strings.name: Emmanuel Macron
strings.role: French politician · President of the Fifth Republic
strings.summary: Macron entered French politics after studying philosophy and public administration and working in public finance and investment banking. He served as deputy secretary-general of the presidency and economy minister, then founded En Marche! He was first elected president in 2017 and re-elected in 2022. Pension reform and the 2024 dissolution of the National Assembly were major policy and decision points that prompted political debate during his presidency.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones from 1977 to 2024. The pension entry describes the arrangements in the 2023 reform and is not a statement of current policy.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Background in philosophy; École nationale d’administration (ENA, 2004)
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Early career
strings.facts.fact-03.value: Inspector of finances, investment banker and economy minister
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Creates a new political movement
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Founded En Marche! in 2016 and won the French presidential election the following year.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Wins two presidential elections
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Elected in 2017 and 2022, becoming the eighth president of France’s Fifth Republic.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Pension reform
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: The 2023 reform provided for a gradual increase in the statutory retirement age from 62 to 64 amid widespread protests.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Announces dissolution of the National Assembly
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Dissolved the National Assembly under Article 12 of the constitution, initiating the process for early parliamentary elections.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Pension reform becomes a political focal point
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The reform law was promulgated with provisions to raise the retirement age gradually, following multiple rounds of nationwide protests.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Re-elected president of France
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Won his second presidential election and began a second term.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: First elected president of France
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Won the presidential election and became the eighth president of the Fifth Republic.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Founds En Marche!
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Created the En Marche! political movement and left his post as economy minister later that year to prepare his campaign.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes economy minister
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Served as minister for the economy, industry and digital affairs until August 2016.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Joins the presidential administration
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became deputy secretary-general of the presidency under François Hollande, taking on a central political role.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Enters investment banking
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Joined Rothschild after four years in the finance inspectorate; returned to the public sector in 2012.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completes administrative training
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduated from the École nationale d’administration and joined the General Inspectorate of Finance, beginning his public-administration career.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Amiens
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Amiens in northern France; later studied philosophy and trained in public administration.
